Designer labels and prized possessions remain coveted, but exclusive experiences, personalised service and privacy are becoming increasingly important. The November 22, 2026 edition examines this shift and the opportunities it creates for luxury businesses.

From Antarctic expeditions and wildlife retreats to immersive dining and personalised wellness programmes, affluent Indians are seeking experiences worth remembering. India’s experiential luxury segment is projected to grow around 20% annually through 2030, with demand spreading beyond the metros. The issue also explores art collecting and why even wealthy Indian buyers remain discerning about value.

In a conversation with Business Today, Jonathan Brinbaum, Managing Director, Watches, Bvlgari, discusses India’s potential as a long-term growth engine for watchmaking, the brand’s retail ambitions and growing interest in women’s mechanical watches.

All this and more in the latest Luxury Issue of Business Today Magazine.</div><a target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" href="https://subscriptions.intoday.in/businesstoday?utm_source=website" class="mag_sld_btn">SUBSCRIBE NOW</a></div></div></div><div class="swiper-slide"><div class="mag_sld_itm"><div class="mag_sld_img"><a href="https://www.businesstoday.in/magazine/issue/2026-11-08" title="2026-11-08"><img width="143" height="196" src="https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/businesstoday/images/issue/whatsapp-image-2026-10-25-at-8.18.47-pm_0.jpeg?size=143:196" alt="" title="" loading="lazy"/></a></div><div class="mag_sld_rhs"><div class="mag_sld_ttl"><a href="https://www.businesstoday.in/magazine/issue/2026-11-08" title="2026-11-08">THE MOST POWERFUL WOMEN IN BUSINESS</a></div><div class="mag_sld_txt">Business Today Magazine’s Most Powerful Women in Business 2026 issue puts sustained profitability and leadership at the centre of its annual rankings. Drawing on an evaluation of nearly 5,500 listed companies, BT MPW 2026 recognises the top 100 women-led enterprises, which together reported profits of ₹2.11 lakh crore in FY26, up 59.4% since FY22. The issue also celebrates exceptional women leading unlisted businesses, start-ups and global organisations.

Beyond the numbers, this year’s special issue explores how women are reshaping India’s family businesses and corporate boardrooms while navigating entrenched biases, challenging traditional hierarchies and building credibility. From carrying forward business legacies to driving transformation, their journeys reflect the growing influence of women across Indian industry.

Business Today Magazine’s BT Most Powerful Women 2026 special issue - Out on stands now</div><a target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" href="https://subscriptions.intoday.in/businesstoday?utm_source=website" class="mag_sld_btn">SUBSCRIBE NOW</a></div></div></div><div class="swiper-slide"><div class="mag_sld_itm"><div class="mag_sld_img"><a href="https://www.businesstoday.in/magazine/issue/2026-10-25" title="2026-10-25"><img width="143" height="196" src="https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/businesstoday/images/issue/22_cover_25-oct-2026_space-ns.jpg?size=143:196" alt="" title="" loading="lazy"/></a></div><div class="mag_sld_rhs"><div class="mag_sld_ttl"><a href="https://www.businesstoday.in/magazine/issue/2026-10-25" title="2026-10-25">INDIA'S SPACE BET</a></div><div class="mag_sld_txt">Business Today Magazine’s latest cover story explores the next phase for India’s private space industry. A generation of start-ups has built on decades of Isro-led investment and the reforms that opened the sector to private enterprise. The launch of Skyroot Aerospace’s Vikram-1, India’s first privately developed orbital-class rocket, marks a major milestone. The harder test now is turning technical progress into sustainable businesses.

The cover story examines what it will take for companies such as Skyroot, Agnikul, Pixxel, Bellatrix and Digantara to scale. They face a thin customer base, gaps in domestic demand and tough competition from SpaceX. As they build their own technology and supply chains, the industry must find repeat customers in India and overseas.

Elsewhere, the issue looks at India’s jobs challenge, where educated young people face scarce entry-level roles even as employers report a shortage of skilled workers. The latest Business Today-C Fore Business Confidence Index also points to cautious hiring and investment plans among companies.

In a conversation with Business Today, Ravi Lambah of Temasek discusses why Indian healthcare remains a “structural, multi-decade opportunity”, including the potential in AI, medtech and digital health, and the need to improve capacity, affordability and access.

All this and more in the latest issue of Business Today Magazine. Out on stands now.

With applications declining, costs rising and employers changing what they expect from management graduates, the degree must show how it can prepare students for a fast-changing business environment. The Business Today–MDRA Best B-Schools 2026-27 edition evaluates 277 participating management institutes across India.

The shift is already visible globally, where several universities have discontinued full-time MBA programmes. In India, schools are promoting one-year executive courses and rethinking how they teach as AI reshapes work and Gen Z weighs alternatives such as specialised master’s degrees, micro-credentials and start-ups. 

The stakes are high for students choosing where to study and how much to invest. Forty per cent of India’s top 25 B-schools reported lower admissions this year than last, including four IIMs. Placement trends also point to changing employer demand, with hiring at the top 25 schools declining while the placement rate rose among schools ranked 51–75. The new rankings place IIM Ahmedabad first, followed by IIM Calcutta, IIM Lucknow, SPJIMR and XLRI.

Collectively, the latest issue captures management education at a turning point: as technology, student expectations and hiring needs evolve, business schools face pressure to make the MBA more relevant, flexible and valuable.
